generation.hypothesis: The concurrent improvement of strength and ductility in HEAs can be achieved through the optimization of alloy composition, processing route, and microstructure.
generation.intervention: Optimization of alloy composition, processing route, and microstructure
generation.conditions: Room temperature or elevated temperature testing
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructure, including grain size, phase composition, and precipitate distribution
generation.mechanism: The optimization of alloy composition, processing route, and microstructure leads to the formation of a favorable microstructure, which in turn enhances the strength and ductility of the HEA. This is achieved through mechanisms such as solid solution strengthening, precipitation strengthening, and grain boundary strengthening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and ductility of the HEA
generation.baseline: As-cast or as-sintered HEA with unoptimized microstructure
generation.boundary: Limitations of the current understanding of HEA microstructure and properties
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the optimization of alloy composition, processing route, and microstructure, as well as the underlying mechanisms governing HEA properties

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic optimization of alloy composition, processing route, and microstructure, followed by testing of mechanical properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized HEA does not exhibit improved strength and ductility, the hypothesis is falsified.

Question: How can the room temperature ductility of an initially brittle refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) with a continuous ordered B2 matrix be improved while maintaining high yield strength?. System: Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr (RHEA). Processing: Condition (1): Cast, hot isostatically pressed (HIPed) at 1200 °C for 2 h, homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h, slow cooled at 10 °C/min. Condition (2): Condition (1) solutionized at 1400 °C for 20 min, water quenched. Condition (3): Condition (2) annealed at 600 °C for 120 hrs, water quenched.. Test conditions: Room temperature (25 °C) and elevated temperature (600 °C) uniaxial compression tests at an initial strain rate of 0.001 s⁻¹.. System: Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 (O-2 HEA), and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98N2 (N-2 HEA). Processing: Arc-melting of pure metals (purity >99.9 wt%), TiN (99.9 wt%), and TiO2 (99.9 wt%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere; remelted at least eight times; drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold (10 mm × 10 mm × 60 mm). Test conditions: Damping measured via multifunction internal friction apparatus at 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0 Hz, temperature range 300–1100 K, heating rate 2 K min⁻¹, max strain amplitude 2 × 10⁻⁴; Tensile tests at room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations.
